<thought>We need to combine the four subnetworks into a single circuit description. Subnet 1 provides two resistors between A‑B and B‑X1. Subnet 2 is a series chain from X1 through N_b1‑N_b2‑N_b3 to X2. Subnet 3 supplies a single resistor value (5 Ω); the most natural way to use it is as a triangle of equal 5 Ω resistors connecting the three main branch terminals X1, X2 and X3. Subnet 4 gives a series chain from B through N_d2‑N_d1 to X3. Putting all of these together yields a complete topology with all nodes and 13 resistors (the two from subnet 1, four from subnet 2, three from the triangle in subnet 3, and three from subnet 4). The final JSON lists each resistor with a unique identifier and its two endpoint nodes.</thought>
